newsitem.title: USA: Amazon.com Web page suffers outage.
newsitem.headline: Amazon.com Web page suffers outage.

text.p: The World Wide Web site of Amazon.com Inc. went down Friday, preventing Internet customers from ordering books from the online retailer.
According to a notice posted on the company's Web page, work was being done on the system and customers should try back later.
A spokesman for Amazon.com was not immediately available to comment on the reason for the outage or how long it would last.

Amazon.com went public last month in one of the hottest offerings of the year, with shares rising as high as $30 before slipping back to the firm's original offering price of $18. On Friday, Amazon.com closed at $19.875, up $1.375.

Though it remains unprofitable, Amazon.com has been one of the more successful ventures to set up shop on the Internet. The two-year-old company, a mail-order operation based in Seattle, publishes a catalog of several million book titles on the Internet and online services.
The company lost about $3 million in the first quarter, but sales are growing quickly. First quarter revenues of $16 million alone outstripped its $15.7 million in sales for all of 1996.
